newsitem.title: CHINA: China state media urges more interest rate changes.
newsitem.headline: China state media urges more interest rate changes.

text.p: China should adjust its interest rates more frequently in 1997 to avoid shocks to the economy, the official China Business Times said on Wednesday.

The central bank, the People's Bank of China, should adjust interest rates two or three times in 1997, with the first change in March or April, the newspaper said. It did not specify whether China should raise or lower interest rates.

China cut interest rates last May and again in August, 1996 to ease credit as inflation fell. The cut last August trimmed bank deposit rates by an average of 1.5 percentage points and lending rates by 1.2 percentage points.
Central bank officials have said recently that the bank considered the current interest level appropriate because the two cuts has achieved the hoped-for results.
Officials have dismissed rumours that the bank planned to cut rates again soon.
The China Business Times urged the central bank to boost supervision of interest rates and monitoring of non-official interest rates.
Future rate adjustments should coincide with interest rates on postal savings and rates on foreign currency deposits, it said. It gave no further details.
